raw_case_text:
We present here the case of a 46-old man, a stockbreeder from the Central Bosnia Canton who was treated for PV endocarditis due to Brucella during 2007. In 1998, he underwent an aortic and mitral mechanical valve replacement surgery due to juvenile rheumatic fever. He was doing well, being work-engaged until 2006, when he started to complain about night sweating, chills, exhaustion, dyspnea, palpitations and chest oppression. At that time he did not measure his body temperature. After more than one year of over repeated hospitalizations at the Department of Internal Medicine of Regional Hospital due to "symptoms of heart failure", he was referred to the Clinic for Infectious Diseases, Clinical Center of Sarajevo University. Upon confirmation of the disease, based on positive blood cultures (B.melitensis) taken during everyday subfebrile temperatures, formerly unrecognized, and on transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) indicative of endocarditis, the patient was transferred to Clinic for Infectious Diseases in Sarajevo.
Upon admission, he had cardiac and extra-cardiac manifestations of endocarditis (systolic-diastolic murmur with absolute arrhythmia, splinter haemorrhages, and laboratory criteria for glomerulonephritis) and symptoms of severe heart failure (class III/IV) according to the New York Heart Association (NYHA) criteria. Standard chest radiography and abdominal ultrasound revealed cardiomegaly, hepatosplenomegaly and stasis in the lungs and liver. Coxiella burnetii coinfection was confirmed by ELISA (enzyme linked immunosorbent assey) test (IgG F2+, IgG F1+, IgA F1+).
Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) confirmed the presence of restenosis, multiple mobile vegetations (5-8 mm) attached to mitral and aortic valve (MV, AV) and signs of severe pulmonary hypertension. He did not respond to quadruple antimicrobial and cardiac therapy. A follow-up TEE performed at the end of the third therapeutic week confirmed progression of the disease: "...persistent multiple mobile vegetations at both valves 7-10 mm, left atrial thrombus 7x10 mm...".

subjective.chief_complaint: A 46-year-old male stockbreeder with mechanical aortic and mitral valves presented with a >1-year history of night sweats, chills, exhaustion, dyspnea, palpitations, chest oppression, and daily subfebrile temperatures.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 46-year-old male stockbreeder from Bosnia who had undergone mechanical aortic and mitral valve replacements in 1998 developed night sweats, chills, severe fatigue, dyspnea, palpitations, chest oppression, and unrecognized daily low-grade fevers starting in 2006. He was hospitalized repeatedly over more than a year at a regional hospital for presumed heart failure before positive blood cultures and TTE prompted transfer to the Sarajevo University Clinic for Infectious Diseases.
subjective.past_medical_history: Mechanical aortic and mitral valve replacement in 1998 for juvenile rheumatic heart disease; occupational exposure as a livestock breeder.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for night sweats, chills, exhaustion, dyspnea, palpitations, chest oppression, and daily subfebrile temperatures.

objective.physical_examination: Subfebrile temperatures, NYHA class III/IV severe congestive heart failure, systolic-diastolic cardiac murmurs with absolute arrhythmia (atrial fibrillation), and peripheral splinter hemorrhages.
objective.routine_investigations: Laboratory evidence of immune-complex glomerulonephritis. Chest X-ray and abdominal ultrasound demonstrated cardiomegaly, pulmonary venous congestion, hepatosplenomegaly, and hepatic congestion. Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) was indicative of prosthetic valve endocarditis.
objective.advanced_workup: Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) revealed prosthetic valve restenosis, multiple mobile vegetations (5-8 mm) attached to both the mechanical mitral and aortic valves, and severe pulmonary hypertension; repeat TEE after 3 weeks of therapy showed disease progression with 7-10 mm vegetations on both valves and a 7 x 10 mm left atrial thrombus.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Serial blood cultures isolated Brucella melitensis and Coxiella burnetii ELISA was concurrently positive for phase I and phase II antibodies (IgG F2+, IgG F1+, IgA F1+), confirming dual-pathogen (Brucella melitensis and Coxiella burnetii) mechanical aortic and mitral prosthetic valve endocarditis complicated by NYHA class III/IV heart failure, glomerulonephritis, and left atrial thrombus. Quadruple antimicrobial therapy and medical heart failure management failed to halt vegetation growth on 3-week follow-up TEE.
